issues.description: Field 'lectureName' has conflicting types between the exercise UML and the reference implementation. In problem_statement.md the UML declares lectureName as type int (line 64: "-lectureName: int"). In the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 6) the field is declared as a String ("private String lectureName;") and all examples (e.g. the example toString in problem_statement.md line 38) and expected getter/setter usage treat lectureName as a String. This mismatch will confuse students about the correct type to implement and can cause compilation/test failures if a student follows the UML and implements lectureName as int instead of String.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML in problem_statement.md so that lectureName is declared as a String (for example: "-lectureName: String"). Also review the surrounding UML/text to ensure the attribute type is consistently shown as String and that example outputs and method descriptions align with String-based getters/setters (getLectureName()/setLectureName(String)).
